name: Prefix-$k$ Littlestone Dimension
definition: Fix $k\ge1$. A **prefix-$k$ Littlestone tree** of depth $d$ is an ordinarily shattered complete binary tree in which the coordinate label is horizontally constant on each of the first $\min\{k,d\}$ levels; after that prefix, labels are unrestricted. The **Prefix-$k$ Littlestone Dimension** $\mathrm{PL}_k(\mathcal{H})$ is the largest depth of such a tree. In particular, $\mathrm{PL}_1=\mathrm{L}$.
graph_summary: Largest shattered tree with a VC-like, level-constant prefix of $k$ queries and an unrestricted tail.
description: Database-defined structural variant; no published origin is claimed.

monotonic.proof: A prefix-constrained shattered tree for a subfamily is still shattered by every containing class, with the same horizontally constant prefix.

p_monotonic.proof: Every coordinate queried by a shattered tree for a projection is retained.  Lift, for each leaf, a projected realizing hypothesis to an original hypothesis; the same prefix-constrained tree is then shattered before projection.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The preceding subfamily and projection arguments establish both required forms of monotonicity.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, so it cannot create a larger prefix-constrained shattered tree.
